 TENDON - task description
 TENDON is used for the calculation of prestressing loads for beam, slabs and shell structures. Essential components of the module are the generation of duct and tendon geometries, the intersection of the ducts with the static system as well as the simulation of the prestressing process and the friction losses.
 The forces of the prestressing are stored as loads on the intersected beam and quad elements in the database.
 Elastic shortening is not considered in TENDON, but can be determined with the corresponding structural analysis modules of SOFiSTiK, especially ASE.
 Important
 The dimensioning of the prestressing is critical for the stability of a prestressed struc- ture. The user of TENDON should therefore convince himself about the accuracy and sensitivity of the prestressing parameters including their effects. A check of the results by means of rough engineering estimates is indispensable.
 1.1 Process in TENDON
 The classical calculation process of TENDON is as follows:
 1. Definition of the prestressing systems (SYSP).
 2. Determination of the reference axes (AXES).
 oa WD
 3. Determination of the duct geometries (TGEO).
 4. Determination of the prestressing sequence (PSIG, PAAS, PFAC or PDEF).
 5. Determination of the tendons and prestressing forces (TEND).
 6. Tabular and graphical output of the reference axes, duct geometries, tendons and pre- stressing forces (ECHO and PLOT).
 In the case of the calculation of flat slabs, there is an alternative input (SLAB), where reference axes, duct geometries and tendons are generated simultaneously.
 1.2 Embedding in the SOFiSTiK process
 In the classical and the graphical environment of SOFiSTiK, it is possible to prestress differ- ent structures with TENDON, e.g., shell structures, beams, flat slabs and bridge structures in CABD (Computer-Aided Bridge Design). Only the prestressing of volume structures is currently not supported.

In the classical and the graphical environment of SOFiSTiK, it is possible to prestress differ- ent structures with TENDON, e.g., shell structures, beams, flat slabs and bridge structures in CABD (Computer-Aided Bridge Design). Only the prestressing of volume structures is currently not supported..
 In the simulation process, TENDON is typically executed after the system generation.
 An exemplary workflow in the CABD environment could look as follows:
 1. Definition of a parametric master cross-section.
 2. Modelling of the global system axis with placements and variables.
 3. Modelling of secondary- and sub-structures.
 oa
 4. Generation of the static system (meshing).
 5. Definition of the prestressing system (TENDON).
 6. Determination of the prestressing geometries along the system axis and evaluation of prestressing loads (TENDON).
 7. Definition of further loads.
 8. Definition of the construction stages.
 9. Calculation and design.
 2 Theoretical principles

Tendons and ducts are usually modelled in an unrolled form along a reference axis. The definition of the tendon is hierarchically based on the following data structures:
 Reference axis The reference axis is the basic geometry on which the constraining points of the duct geometry are defined. The reference axis can be taken from another programme (e.g. SOFiMSHC, SOFiPLUS) or can be created in TENDON. Several ducts can refer to the same reference axis.
 Duct The duct geometry is usually defined relative to the reference axis with u- and v-values, but can also be generated with an existing curve. A duct can contain several tendons.
 Tendon Tendon geometries are defined on duct geometries. The difference between tendon and duct geometry is that (i) the tendon can be defined only on a section of the duct and (ii) it can have an eccentricity with respect to the duct geometry.

When describing tendons, three different coordinate systems can be distinguished (see Figure 2.1):
 Global coordinate system The orientation of the global coordinate system is defined during system generation (e.g. in SOFiMSHC or SOFiPLUS). It must be described as a Cartesian coordinate system with the Z-axis usually pointing in the di- rection of gravity (downwards).
 Local coordinate system For curved reference axes, the local coordinate system can vary along the curve. The origin is at the corresponding point S on the reference axis and the local x-direction points in the tangential direction. The local y- and z- axes are orthogonal and are defined differently depending on how the reference axis was created:
 • Beam sequence: For the case that the reference axis was created with beams, the reference axis is orthogonal to the beam cross-sections and the local y- and z-directions are defined according to the cross-sectional coordinate system.
 •
 3D curve: If the reference axis was defined with a 3D curve, the y- and z-axis are referred to the global coordinates. Usually the local z-axis lies on the plane spanned by the local x-axis and the global Z-axis.
 Local coordinates U or V always refer to the local y- or z-axis of the coordi- nate system of the reference axis.
 Element coordinate system The prestressing loads are stored in the respective coordinate system of the elements. In the case of beams, this is the cross-sectional coordinate system, which is normally identical to the local coordinate system
 of the reference axis.

The table defines:

   - **`OFFN`**: *Limit distance for intersections in normal direction*.

The table defines the **GEOX** record, which controls **exporting geometry of a duct or tendon** for further use (e.g., detailed design). It specifies **which geometry is exported**, **which portion of the curve**, **how output points are sampled**, and **how the results are formatted and delivered**.

## Columns
Each row has:
- **Item**: the keyword/parameter name used in the GEOX record
- **Description**: meaning and constraints
- **Unit**: data type/physical unit (or categorical type)
- **Default**: default behavior when not explicitly set

## Parameters and their roles

### NOG
- **Item**: `NOG`
- **Meaning**: Identifier of the duct geometry or tendon geometry (referenced via `TYPG`).
- **Unit**: `–`
- **Default**: `!` (mandatory)
- **Context**: If `TYPG` is `DUCT`, `NOG` points to **TGEO**; if `TYPG` is `TEND`, `NOG` points to **TEND**.

### FROM / TO
- **Items**: `FROM`, `TO`
- **Meaning**: Start and end station along the reference axis for exporting a **sub-segment** of the curve.
- **Unit**: `–` (stations are typically numerical station values)
- **Default**: `*` (meaning: *by default the whole curve is output*)
- **Constraint (from context)**: Multiple GEOX records can export **section by section** using `FROM/TO` with different sampling increments, but **all other values must be identical** and **segments must be in ascending order**.

### INC
- **Item**: `INC`
- **Meaning**: Controls output point sampling along the station range.
  - `> 0`: distance between output points
  - `< 0`: number of output points
- **Unit**: `–`
- **Default**: `0.5`
- **Purpose**: Determines the resolution of exported geometry.

### TYPG
- **Item**: `TYPG`
- **Meaning**: Type of geometry to export.
  - `DUCT`: duct geometry
  - `TEND`: tendon geometry
- **Unit**: `LIT4`
- **Default**: `DUCT`
- **Default implication**: If not set, the record exports duct geometry.

### OUTP
- **Item**: `OUTP`
- **Meaning**: Output scope definition using one or multiple literals.
- **Unit**: `LIT`
- **Default**: `SUVXYZ`
- **Options (from context)**:
  - `S`: station along reference axis
  - `U`: local y-direction distance from reference axis
  - `V`: local z-direction distance from reference axis
  - `X, Y, Z`: 3D coordinates of tendon/duct
- **Behavior**: Each literal creates its own column in the output file; in “other export cases” it indicates which parameters are printed.

### CSP
- **Item**: `CSP`
- **Meaning**: Reference to a **cross-section point**. When set, `U` and `V` refer to the CSP instead of the reference axis.
- **Unit**: `LIT4`
- **Default**: `-` (not referenced)
- **Remark (from context)**: If no CSP is found at a station, `u` and `v` fall back to reference-axis-based values.

### DU / DV
- **Items**: `DU`, `DV`
- **Meaning**: Offset in local coordinates:
  - `DU`: local y-direction offset
  - `DV`: local z-direction offset
- **Unit**: `[m]1001` (meters)
- **Default**: `0.0` for both

### FACH
- **Item**: `FACH`
- **Meaning**: Superelevation factor. Applies only to `u` and `v` coordinates:
  - Une = (Uod + DU) · FACH (as given in context)
- **Unit**: `–`
- **Default**: `1.0`
- **Effect**: Scales the influence of offsets on u/v output coordinates.

### EXPO
- **Item**: `EXPO`
- **Meaning**: Destination/format of exported curve output.
- **Unit**: `LIT4`
- **Default**: `PLB`
- **Options (from context)**:
  - `TXT`: text file (commonly “.uv”)
  - `GAX`: database geometry axis
  - `PLB`: into report
  - `CSV`: `.csv` file
- **File naming (from context)**: default filename uses `project-name + _GEOX_ + AXID`, or if `AXID` is not set, `projectname + _GEOX_ + NRG`.

### AXID
- **Item**: `AXID`
- **Meaning**: Identifier of the new output axis.
- **Unit**: `LIT4`
- **Default**: `*`
- **Constraint (from context)**: **Mandatory for output to database** (`EXPO GAX`).

### TITL
- **Item**: `TITL`
- **Meaning**: Title of the output.
- **Unit**: `LIT32`
- **Default**: `-`

### SEP
- **Item**: `SEP`
- **Meaning**: Separator for decimal numbers in TXT/CSV output.
- **Unit**: `LIT4`
- **Default**: `COMA`
- **Options (from context)**:
  - `COMA`: separation with comma (1.00m)
  - `DOT`: separation with dot (1.00m)

### Table overview: *SYSS – Prestressing system for pre-tensioning* (tendon system definition)

This table defines the input parameters for a **pre-tensioning prestressing system** (SYSS). The SYSS record is described as a **simplification of the SYSP record** specifically for **pre-tensioning tendons**. It contains the key properties required to model the tendon geometry and force transfer behavior, with special attention to the friction/wobble parameters and the tendon’s cross-sectional and layout properties. The record requires a **tendon-specific setup** and is intended to be used within a prestressing model; values are later referenced by reporting features such as **force distribution** (e.g., ECHO TEND / PLOT FACT).

A critical compatibility note in the surrounding context is that when using **SYSS**, it is expected that the **construction phases for installation (ICS1) and grouting (ICS2) of the CS record** are identical. Also, since older workflows relied on copying from existing tendon system entries, the record emphasizes that tendon procedure maintenance/QA is extensive and that such broad legacy support is no longer provided.

---

### Columns

- **Item**: Parameter name (keyword) used in the SYSS record.
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning of the parameter.
- **Unit**: Declared unit (often with reference/clarity hints using bracketed indexing like `[kN]1028`).
- **Default**: Default value where defined; otherwise marked as required (`!`).

---

### Parameters and their roles

**1) System identification / selection**
- **NOPS**: “Id of the prestressing system”. No unit; required.

**2) Material and force reference basis**
- **MAT**: “Material number of the prestressing steel”. No unit; required.
- **ZV**: “Reference force”. Unit shown as **[kN]**. Required.  
  Context explains that ZV is needed for inputs like **“Prestressing limits with factors” PFAC** and for the reported force distribution. A “sensible value” is the **prestressing force after anchor set (Pm0)**, but the user may set it arbitrarily.

**3) Tendon geometry and composition**
- **AZ**: Steel area of the tendon (sum for all wires/strands). Unit **[mm²]**; required.
- **LITZ**: Number of wires/strands. Default **1**.

**4) Curvature constraints**
- **MINR**: Minimum permissible curvature radius. Unit **[m]**; required.

**5) Friction / wobble behavior**
- **BETA**: Wobble coefficient. Unit **[deg/m]**; required.  
  Context highlights that using a wrong unit for β can lead to deviations from reference solutions; default Tendon convention is **[◦/m]**, while standards may express it as **[1/m]** or **[1/ƒt]**. If the corresponding unit is specified, conversion may not be necessary.
- **BETG**: Wobble coefficient for straight PT SV geometries. Same unit as BETA; default is **BET A**.
- **MUE**: Friction coefficient for stressing. Required.
- **MUEE-**: Friction coefficient for releasing. Default **MUE**.

**6) Eccentricity and spacing constraints (duct interaction)**
- **ECC**: Maximum eccentricity of tendon inside duct. Unit **[mm]**; default **0.0**.
- **CDIS**: Minimum distance between ducts. Unit **[mm]**; default **0.0**.
- **CEDG**: Minimum distance between duct and boundary. Unit **[mm]**; default **0.0**.

**7) Jacking/anchorage deformation model (pre-tensioning related)**
- **SP**: Slip at the jacking anchor. Unit **[mm]**; required.
- **SF**: Additional elongations. Unit **[mm]**; default **0.0**.
- **LPRE**: Straight at the jacking anchor. Unit **[mm]**; default **0.50**.
- **LFIX**: Straight at the dead anchor. Unit **[mm]**; default **LPRE**.

**8) Duct geometry**
- **DO**: Outer diameter of the duct. Unit **[mm]**; required.

**9) Title / labeling**
- **TITI**: Title of the prestressing system. Default **LIT32**.

The SYSS record is described as a **simplification of the SYSP record** specifically for **pre-tensioning**, and it is intended to reduce the effort compared to the more general SYSP definition for post-tensioning / jacking scenarios. The record depends on the overall construction model: when using SYSS, the **construction phases for installation (ICS1) and grouting (ICS2) of the CS record are expected to be identical**.

For the SYSS system, general parameters related to prestressing force reference values and tendon geometry/distribution are defined through the listed items. In addition, the surrounding context states that older workflows (selecting existing tendon systems from a bridge construction table) are **no longer supported**, and therefore this record is the supported method to represent the tendon system parameters consistently for maintenance and quality assurance.

---

   - **Default:** “!” mandatory.

5. **LITZ — Number of wires/strands**  
   - **Meaning:** Count of individual wires/strands that make up the tendon system.  
   - **Unit:** none (– not explicitly given)  
   - **Default:** **1**.

6. **TITLE — Title of the prestressing system**  
   - **Meaning:** Descriptive label for the tendon system.  
   - **Unit:** none (–)  
   - **Default:** **LITZ2** (i.e., tied to the naming/labeling conventions).

The table documents the **AXES** input record used to define a **reference axis** for duct (or related geometry) generation in a structural modelling system. Each record corresponds to one segment or specification of the axis; multiple AXES records of the same **TYPE** can be chained to build a complete reference axis.

**Primary identifier and metadata**
- **NOH (Id of the reference axis)**: Unique axis ID. Unit is “–”; default shown as **1**.
- **TITL (Title of the Reference Axis)**: Descriptive name, up to **32 characters**; default shown as “–” (none).

**Axis definition method (TYPE)**
- **TYPE (Type of definition)** determines how the axis geometry is described. The default is **NODE**.
  - **BEAM**: Axis defined by a **sequence of beam elements**. Input parameters correspond to a range “from – to – delt”.
  - **NODE**: Axis defined by a **sequence of nodes** (also “from – to – delt”).
  - **AUTO**: Axis defined by **start and end node/beam element**; intermediate beam elements are automatically found, sorted, and assembled into a coherent sequence. Input is “from – to”.
  - **REFX**: Axis is taken from an **externally defined geometry axis** created in another module (e.g., GAX). The axis ID is supplied in **VAL1**, and an optional **secondary axis identifier (A–Z)** can be supplied in **VAL2**.
  - **SLN**: Axis runs along previously created **structural lines** (e.g., from SOFiMSHC SLN / SOFiPLUS). Several SLN axis records can be specified consecutively to cover multiple structural lines.

**Values (VAL1–VAL3)**
The table’s **VAL1**, **VAL2**, **VAL3** fields are context-dependent and must follow the selected **TYPE**:
- **VAL1**
  - For **BEAM**/**NODE**: “from – …” start index/range value.
  - For **AUTO**: start index/identifier.
  - For **REFX**: **Id of geometry axis** (and possibly the referenced axis ID).
  - For **SLN**: **Id of structural line**.
  - For **POLY**: begins the **XYZ polygon coordinates**.
- **VAL2**
  - For **BEAM**: “to” and **delt** handling is done via VAL2/VAL3 depending on the format; default delt is **1** for BEAM sequences.
  - For **NODE**: similarly “to” and step (**delt** default **1**).
  - For **AUTO**: end index/identifier.
  - For **REFX**: **secondary axis** identifier (A–Z).
  - For **POLY**: second coordinate component **Y**.
- **VAL3**
  - For **BEAM**: “delt” (step size).
  - For **NODE**: “delt” (step size).
  - For **POLY**: third coordinate component **Z**.
Notes implied by the description: **POLY** uses repeated AXES records to enter consecutive polygon course points via **X–Y–Z** coordinates (VAL1→VAL3 per point).

**Prestressing element selection (KIND)**
- **KIND (Kind of prestressed elements)** controls which element types the duct curve is allowed to intersect or target for prestressing:
  - **BEAM**: only beam elements are prestressed/considered.
  - **QUAD**: only quad elements.
  - **AUTO**: both beam and quad elements.
Default is **BEAM**. The selection logic (from the text): duct curve runs **inside** or **least outside** the selected elements.
Important override behavior: the **underlying AXES KIND can be overwritten** later by other records such as **TGEO ELEM**, enabling intersections with different element types than originally defined (e.g., defining via KIND BEAM but later intersecting quads).

**Station parameter (S)**
- **S (Start station)**: start station along the axis. Default **0.00**. Only the first record’s value is used when multiple records form the axis.

Overall, the table specifies how to configure the **reference axis** using one of several **TYPE** strategies (BEAM, NODE, AUTO, REFX, SLN, POLY), how the corresponding **VAL fields** must be populated, and how **KIND** determines eligible element types for prestressing—optionally modifiable via downstream geometry settings.

A reference axis can be divided into spans **only once**, and each resulting span has a **referenced length of 1.0** (i.e., the span is normalized for internal reference).

### Items and meaning
**NOH**  
- **Description:** Identifier of the **reference axis** to which the TOPP definition applies.  
- **Unit:** none (shown as “–”).  
- **Default:** “!” indicates there is **no default**; it is mandatory.

**KIND**  
- **Description:** Specifies the **type of the given point** that follows in the line. Valid kinds are:
  - **NODE:** beam node points.
  - **REFX:** stations (coordinates) **on the reference axis**.
  - **S:** position of the top position (as used with TOPP; further interpretation depends on context and KIND usage).
- **Unit / Default:**  
  - **Default shown:** not fixed in the table (“!” behavior).

Practically, the KIND value must match what the subsequent coordinate fields represent.

**S** (listed as a separate item)  
- **Description:** The **position of the top position**. It is used in conjunction with KIND to indicate where the “top” point lies relative to the reference axis.  
- **Unit:** “–” (not explicitly given; it is coordinate-based in the TOPP examples).  
- **Default:** “!” (mandatory / no default).

**SP**  
- **Description:** **Span position** used to start a new span or terminate the preceding span.  
  - **SP must be an ascending integer**, except the **last value may be negative** to express the end-of-span/cantilever geometry case.

This table defines a **group attribute control** used to manage which *element groups* participate in subsequent **duct curve intersection** logic, specifically records that must be provided **before `TGEO`**. The table contains two rows describing the **items/fields** that make up a **`GRP` record**, along with their meaning, expected unit/type, and defaults.

#### Fields

1. **`NO` (Number of the group)**
   - **Purpose:** Specifies which group is targeted by the `GRP` record.
   - **Semantics:**  
     - The table states the default for `NO` is **`ALL`**, meaning that, unless otherwise restricted, the command applies to *all groups*.
     - `NO` can represent different group identification schemes depending on system conventions:
       - **Primary groups** are defined by a **number** (e.g., `100`, `200`).
       - **Secondary groups** are defined by a **literal/string** (e.g., `'SEC1'`).
       - A special value **`ALL`** is used to apply the selection to *all groups* (enable/disable all).
   - **Format/Type:** Shown as `–/LIT4`.
     - The dash indicates it is not tied to a physical unit; `LIT4` indicates a literal or token-like parameter of length/type consistent with the grammar.

2. **`CMD` (Command)**
   - **Purpose:** Controls whether the specified group(s) are **enabled** or **disabled**.
   - **Allowed values:**
     - **`ON`**: Enable the group.
     - **`OFF`**: Disable the group.
   - **Default:** **`ON`**, meaning that if a group is referenced without explicitly setting `CMD`, it is activated.

#### Units / Defaults column usage
- The **Unit** column is **non-physical** (e.g., `–/LIT4` and `LIT4`), indicating these are **syntax/parameter types** rather than measurement units.
- The **Default** column provides:
  - `NO` defaults to **`ALL`**
  - `CMD` defaults to **`ON`**

#### Behavioral context (from accompanying notes)
- A key operational rule is that this `GRP` record is an **attribute record** and **must precede `TGEO`**.
- The selection defined by `GRP` determines which elements a duct curve (`TGEO`) can intersect:
  - Using primary group numbers enables intersection with those primary groups only.
  - Using `NO 'ALL' CMD ON` enables intersection with all groups.
  - Disabling a secondary group (e.g., `GRP NO 'SEC1' CMD OFF`) prevents intersection with that secondary group.

In summary, the table specifies the minimal schema for `GRP`: choose the target group via `NO` (number, literal, or `ALL`) and control its participation via `CMD` (ON/OFF), with defaults that enable all groups unless restricted.

The table describes the record fields used in the **TGEO** input to define a **duct geometry** for tendon prestressing. Each TGEO record is identified and linked to other model entities, and it also controls which structural element types the duct curve applies to.

### Key identifiers
- **NOG** (Id of the duct geometry): Specifies the unique ID of the duct geometry being defined in this TGEO record. Unit: “–”. No default (mandatory).
- **NOH** (Id of the reference axis): Specifies the ID of the **reference axis** that the duct geometry is related to. The duct curve is defined relative to this axis. Unit: “–”. No default (mandatory).
- **NOPS** (Id of the prestressing system): Specifies which prestressing system the duct belongs to. Unit: “–”. No default (mandatory).

### Geometry source / curve reference
- **XREF** (Reference to existing geometry): Optional linkage to an **already defined external curve**. If XREF is provided, the duct geometry curve is taken from an existing geometry (e.g., a curve defined earlier in another module) and adapted to the stationing of the reference axis. Unit: `LIT4` (logical/text input length as defined by the system). Default: none (field present only when needed).  
  *Context note:* For compatibility, TGEO may contain additional undocumented items; when using those items, the record name (e.g., `NOPS 42`) must be explicitly written.

### Prestressed element selection control
- **ELEM** (Kind of prestressed elements): Controls which FE element types are considered for prestressing based on the duct curve location. Unit: `LIT4`. Default: **AXES**.
  - **AXES**: Use the element type selection as defined by the reference axis (from the **AXES** record). This can be overridden here.
  - **BEAM**: Prestress **only beam** elements.
  - **QUAD**: Prestress **only quad** elements.
  - **AUTO**: Allow prestressing of **beam and quad** elements.

The accompanying context explains the selection rule: the elements are those for which the **duct curve runs inside** or at least **least outside** the element.

### Metadata / display
- **TITI** (**TITL**) (Title of the duct geometry): Human-readable name for the duct geometry. Limited to **max. 32 characters**. Unit: `LIT32`. Default: none.  
- **GUID** (128 bit code as hexadecimal string): Globally unique identifier for the record. Unit: `LIT36`. Default: none.

Overall, this TGEO field set defines: *which duct geometry (NOG) is built for which prestressing system (NOPS) and reference axis (NOH), whether to use an external curve (XREF) or an internal curve definition, which element types are eligible for prestressing (ELEM), and how the record is labeled (TITL) and uniquely identified (GUID).*

The input table documents the **PTUV** record used in spline duct geometry modelling. PTUV defines one **constraining point** of the spline duct and is entered after **TGEO**. Multiple constraining points are provided by repeating PTUV records, enabling the duct geometry to be guided by those points along a reference axis. The table specifies, for each PTUV field, its meaning, unit, and default behavior.

### Table structure
It contains columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**.  
Most fields have default “–” (no automatic value), indicating they must be supplied when relevant for the chosen configuration.

### Fields and meanings
- **TYPE**: Defines how the point’s axial location is interpreted. Allowed values are:
  - **NODE**: a beam node number
  - **BEAM**: a beam element; additionally requires a relative position **X** on the element
  - **SPAN**: span position (only if TOPP created spans along the reference axis)
  - **REFX**: station on the reference axis  
  The default shown is **BEAM**.

- **S**: The input position according to **TYPE**. Default is **0.0**.  
  This is the primary axial coordinate along the reference axis (or beam/span/node depending on TYPE).

- **X**: Local x-coordinate used only when **TYPE = BEAM**. It denotes relative position along the beam element with **X ∈ [0, bem]** (bem = beam length). Default **0.0**.

- **CSP**: Cross-section point reference (e.g., created earlier in AQUA). If specified, it shifts the origin of the PTUV local coordinate system from the reference axis station to the cross-section point; consequently **U** and **V** are measured relative to CSP. Default is “–”.

- **U / V**: Local coordinates of the constraining point in the **local coordinate system**:
  - **U**: horizontal offset in the local **y-direction**
  - **V**: vertical offset in the local **z-direction**  
  Their units are given as length (**[m]** with exponent annotation in the table). No default values are provided.

- **DUS / DVS** (table shows **DUS** and **DVS** as separate items): Inclinations defining how the local coordinate system (or guiding line) behaves:
  - **DUS**: inclination in local y-direction
  - **DVS**: inclination in local z-direction  
  Defaults are “–”.

- **DL / DR**: Straight line segment extents replacing curved duct geometry:
  - **DL**: left segment length in negative s-direction (negative direction along reference axis)
  - **DR**: right segment length in positive direction  
  Units are length; default “–”.

- **RH / RV**: Radius specifications for curvature smoothing in the horizontal/vertical construction planes:
  - **RH**: horizontal radius
  - **RV**: vertical radius  
  The table’s accompanying text explains that these radius lengths are chosen to make transitions to neighboring constraining points as straight as possible. Default “–”.

- **RL**: Influence length of the radius. The notes indicate this may also be specified manually, but unsuitable values can cause strong curvature at arc ends. Default “–”.

- **KIND**: Specifies the point type when a straight segment is required:
  - **PRES**: “jacking anchor” (straight-line segment generated with length controlled by system parameter such as SYSP LPRE)
  - **FIX**: “dead anchor” (straight-line segment generated with length controlled by SYSP LFIX)  
  The record excerpt in the prompt mentions **FIX** as a “Dead anchor.” Default is **LIT4** (table’s default representation), with the option values PRES/FIX described.

### Conceptual note for RAG context
The table implies that PTUV combines:
1) axial placement (**TYPE**, **S**, and sometimes **X**),  
2) cross-section-based local positioning (**CSP**, **U**, **V**),  
3) tangent/shape control via inclinations and geometric blending (**DUS/DVS**, **DL/DR**, **RH/RV**, **RL**), and  
4) special straight-segment behavior via **KIND** (PRES/FIX).

The table describes the input fields for **PTSV**, a record used to define **constraining points** of a **polygonal duct geometry** (typically for external tendons with bending blocks). In this context, **PTSV must be entered after TGEO**, and **multiple constraining points are created by repeating PTSV** entries. Each constraining point represents the **tangent intersection position between two duct segments**, where the duct geometry is rounded via a **bending block**.

### Record structure and parameters
The table’s first field is **TYPE**, which specifies how the point’s position is referenced:

- **NODE**: position at a beam node.
- **BEAM**: position along a beam element, additionally requiring a **relative position** parameter **X**.
- **SPAN**: position along a span (only possible if, with **TOPP**, spans were created along the reference axis).
- **REFX**: station on the reference axis.

The **default TYPE is BEAM**, and the table indicates the default for the record’s meaning of *S* (see below).

### Positioning along the duct reference
- **S**: *“Input according to TYPE”*; it is the main position coordinate.
  - The table lists a **default of 0.0**.
  - For TYPE = **NODE**, S identifies the node number.
  - For TYPE = **BEAM**, S identifies the beam element position along the reference axis, while **X** specifies the relative point location along the beam element itself.
  - For TYPE = **SPAN**, S is a span position.
  - For TYPE = **REFX**, S is the station on the reference axis.

- **X** (only for TYPE = **BEAM**): **Local x-coordinate** / **relative position on the beam element**.
  - The units shown are meters with a beam-length scaling indicator.
  - The table notes the default **0.0**.
  - Conceptually, it constrains **X to the beam element extent** (described in the context as \(X \in [0, bem]\)).

### Local duct coordinates (cross-sectional offset)
The table then defines the local coordinates of the constraining point within the duct’s reference system (local coordinate system of the reference axis):
- **U**: **Local y-coordinate** (horizontal position within the local system).
- **V**: **Local z-coordinate** (vertical position within the local system).

These values determine where the constraining point lies laterally/vertically relative to the reference axis (see local coordinate system description in the context). Defaults are not explicitly given in the table for U and V.

### Bending block geometry
The duct rounding at each constraining point is governed by:
- **R**: **Radius of the bending**.
  - Unit: meter.
  - **Default: MINR**, where MINR is taken from the prestressing system **SYSP** and represents the minimum allowed radius.

- **BLCK**: **Length of the bending block** (unit meter).

The context specifies processing rules for how R and BLCK interact:
- If both are not given appropriately, **R may be set to MINR**, and BLCK is determined.
- If R is greater than MINR, BLCK can be determined; if BLCK is too small, R may be reduced to MINR.
- The system may **widen the block** or **recompute BLCK** to satisfy constraints.

### Point type: PRES vs FIX
Finally:
- **KIND**: **Kind of point** (defaults to LIT4, i.e., a listed default option rather than a numeric default).
  - **PRES**: *Jacking anchor*
  - **FIX**: *Dead anchor*

If **KIND** is specified as **PRES** or **FIX**, a **straight line segment** is generated on the duct geometry. The lengths of these straight segments are defined in **SYSP LPRE** (for PRES) or **SYSP LFIX** (for FIX).

### Overall geometric behavior (polygonal vs spline)
The context emphasizes that with **polygonal geometry using PTSV**, the 3D duct curve is constructed **directly from constraining points**, so the connection between two constraining points remains **straight even if the reference axis is curved**. This differs from spline duct geometry using PTUV, which involves prior unrolling into horizontal/vertical planes.

The table defines **FRIC** (friction) as an **attribute record** that must be provided **before `TEND`** in the input sequence. Its purpose is to apply **additional friction in a specific station interval**. The record modifies friction behavior in a localized region; if the FRIC record is given **without parameters**, all involved values are internally reset to the system’s default friction settings.

Importantly, the friction inputs in this record are processed **analogously to `SYSP BETA` and `BETG`**, and are **explicitly stated not to influence tendon geometry**. Instead, they affect the mechanical behavior related to friction between tendon and conduit/contact surface.

### Interval control (FROM / TO)
- **FROM**: Station of the **start** of the friction region.  
  - Unit: `–` (stationless internal reference)  
  - Default: `0`
- **TO**: Station of the **end** of the friction region.  
  - Unit: `–`  
  - Default: `0`

Together, `FROM` and `TO` define the **range along the alignment** where the additional friction parameters are active. If both remain at defaults, the interval may effectively be null or default-handled by the system.

### Friction wobble parameters (BETA / BETE)
- **BETA**: Additional “wobble” at the **begin** of the friction interval.  
  - Unit: `[deg/m]`  
  - Default: `0`
- **BETE**: Additional “wobble” at the **end** of the friction interval.  
  - Unit: `[deg/m]`  
  - Default: `BETA`  
  - Meaning: If `BETE` is not explicitly set, it inherits the same value as `BETA`, implying a uniform additional wobble over the interval.

These parameters represent the extra angular deviation rate affecting frictional losses (wobble/friction modeling), interpolated or applied between the interval boundaries.

### Superposition type (TYPE)
- **TYPE** specifies how the additional wobble/friction quantity is combined with existing values:
  - Unit: `–`
  - Default: `ADD`
  - Supported values:
    - **ADD** (additive superposition):  
      \[
      \beta_{exist} + \beta_{add}
      \]
      where the system adds the additional contribution to the existing one.
    - **VECT** (vectorial superposition):  
      \[
      \sqrt{\beta_{exist}^2 + \beta_{add}^2}
      \]
      where the additional effect is combined via a root-sum-square formulation.

### Record usage context / dependencies
This record is an **attribute record** that must be stated **before `TEND`**. It also references a usage pattern seen in the example text:  
`FRIC FROM 10.0 TO 15.0 BETA 0.005[1/m] TYPE ADD`  
which indicates applying additional friction (wobble) between stations **10.0 and 15.0**, using **additive** superposition. (The example’s unit notation may vary, but the table defines BETA/BETE as `[deg/m]`.)

The input table defines an attribute record for **PSIG** (prestressing parameters) used to prescribe tendon prestressing behaviour and associated stress limits. It is meant to be supplied **before TEND** and, by design, it **overwrites previously set attribute records** such as **PFAC, PSIG, PAAS, or PDEF**. For **two-sided prestressing**, the framework supports specifying a **different prestressing sequence** for the second side via another PSIG record; in that case, only the **ANWS** value is updated, while the **k-values and KAPA** are not changed.

### Core fields and meaning

- **KIND** (default: **RI**)  
  Encodes the **type/order of prestressing** with enumerated options:  
  - **RI**: prestressing from right  
  - **LE**: prestressing from left  
  - **RILE**: first from right, then from left  
  - **LERI**: first from left, then from right  
  This determines which side(s) are tensioned and in what order.

- **ANWS** (default: **TS**) Prestressing sequence  
  Specifies the desired sequence using either literals or a **bit-mask**:  
  - **T / 1** = Stressing  
  - **R / 2** = Releasing  
  - **W / 4** = Re-stressing  
  - **S / 8** = Slip  
  The default **“TS”** corresponds to **Stressing + Slip** = T + S.

- **KAPA** (default: marked with *; described as safety friction factor κ)  
  Represents the **friction safety factor** used to prevent overstress. A key regulation note states that, per the German national annex, the **maximum jacking force** must be reduced. If **no value** is given, it is taken from the national annex. Special rules include:  
  - **0.0 disables** the consideration of the safety factor.  
  - An entry flagged as “not allowed” is replaced by the national annex value.

- **KAPL** (default: **SYMM**) Influence length of KAPA for two-sided prestressing  
  Controls how much tendon is considered when applying the KAPA reduction on the second side:  
  - **SYMM** (Symmetrical): the entire tendon is considered, causing the **same reduction** on both sides.  
  - **OPT** (Optimised): only the tendon segment where **additional forces are applied** is considered, yielding **lower reduction** on the second side. If optimisation has no solution, the system assumes a **symmetric reduction**.

### Stress limit parameters (k-values)

The table then lists **K1–K8**, which define stress limits relative to characteristic material strengths. Their defaults are indicated by **\***, meaning they are typically derived from standard values if not directly specified.

- **K1**: *Maximum stress during tensioning* (default *)  
- **K2**: used to compute  
  \[
  \sigma_{p,\max}=\min\left(K1\cdot f_{pk},\;K2\cdot f_{p0,1k}\right)
  \]
- **K3**: *General stress limit after anchor set*  
- **K4**: used to compute  
  \[
  \sigma_{pm0}=\min\left(K3\cdot f_{pk},\;K4\cdot f_{p0,1k}\right)
  \]
- **K5**: *Stress limit at jacking anchor*  
- **K6**:  
  \[
  \sigma_{jack}=\min\left(K5\cdot f_{pk},\;K6\cdot f_{p0,1k}\right)
  \]
- **K7**: *Stress limit at dead anchor*  
- **K8**:  
  \[
  \sigma_{dead}=\min\left(K7\cdot f_{pk},\;K8\cdot f_{p0,1k}\right)
  \]

### Interpretation rules for k-values

Although Eurocode-related terminology is used (K1/K2/K3/K4, etc.), the system notes that **historical numbering differs from Eurocode**. Additionally, the table context explains two regimes:

- If **k < 10**, values are treated as **factors** multiplying ultimate strength \(f_{pk}\) (or yield strength \(f_{p0,1k}\)).  
- If **k ≥ 10**, values are treated as **direct stress limits**; in this case, the corresponding alternative second values are not used.  
For manual direct stress/force input, it recommends using **PDEF** instead of PFAC/PSIG-style k-values.

Overall, the table provides a structured way to control prestressing order (**KIND**), stressing history (**ANWS**), friction safety behaviour (**KAPA**, **KAPL**), and the resulting allowable stress checks at key prestressing stages (**K1–K8**), with strong precedence rules relative to other related attribute records.

The table defines the **PAAS** input record used to control **prestressing sequence** and the associated **stress limits** for post-tensioning. It is an **attribute record** that must be provided **before TEND**; as stated in the surrounding context, it **overwrites previously set attribute records** (PFAC, PSIG, PAAS, PDEF). For **two-sided prestressing**, a second PAAS record may be supplied to specify a **different prestressing sequence for the second side**; in that case, **only ANWS is updated**, while the **k-values** (K1–K3) remain unchanged.

### Columns
- **Item**: Field name within the PAAS record.
- **Description**: Meaning of each field and how it is interpreted.
- **Unit**: Unit column is present; for most fields it is shown as a dash (–), implying either dimensionless ratios or stress inputs are handled in the model’s prevailing units.
- **Default**: Default values and guidance on required inputs.

### Field definitions
**1) KIND (default: RI) – Type of prestressing**
Specifies from which side prestressing acts and whether it occurs sequentially:
- **RI**: Prestressing from the **right**
- **LE**: Prestressing from the **left**
- **RILE**: Prestressing **first from right, then from left**
- **LE RI**: Prestressing **first from left, then from right**
(“LEBRI” in the image appears to be “LERI”.)

**2) ANWS (default: TS) – Prestressing sequence**
Defines the operational order of stressing-related phases using a combination of literals or a numeric **bit mask**:
- **1 or T**: **Stressing**
- **2 or R**: **Releasing**
- **4 or W**: **Re-stressing**
- **8 or S**: **Slip**
The default **TS** corresponds to “Stressing + Slip”. Alternatively, the sequence can be encoded as a sum, e.g. **1 + 8 = 9** for “Stressing + Slip”. The context notes that, in two-sided cases, PAAS on the second side can modify **ANWS only** (not K-values).

**3) K1 (default: “!” i.e., must be provided) – Stress limit prior to seating**
Represents the maximum stress before seating occurs:
- \( \sigma_{max} = k1 \cdot f_{py} (= k1 \cdot f_{p0,1k}) \)

**4) K2 (default: “!” i.e., must be provided) – Stress limit at anchorages**
Stress limit when transfer to anchorages occurs:
- \( \sigma_{anchor} = k2 \cdot f_{pu} (= k2 \cdot f_{pk}) \)

**5) K3 (default: “!” i.e., must be provided) – General stress limit after anchor set**
Stress limit after the anchorage is set:
- \( \sigma_{onsist} = k3 \cdot f_{pu} (= k3 \cdot f_{pk}) \)

### Overall behavior and examples (from context)
- Example formats show PAAS records like:  
  `PAAS KIND RI ANWS 15 K1 0.9 K2 0.7 K3 0.74`
- Another example allows changing the sequence for the second side by adding another PAAS record with the same K-values but different **ANWS**.
- The table therefore captures both the **sequence control (KIND, ANWS)** and the **stress limit scaling factors (K1–K3)** required for the prestressing process.

The table describes the **PFAC** record, which is an *attribute record* used to define prestressing-related **force factors** for a subsequent tendon/sequence definition. It is explicitly required that **PFAC must be specified prior to TEND**; each PFAC entry **overwrites all previously set attribute records** from **PFAC, PSIG, PAAS, or PDEF**. For compatibility, PFAC may contain additional undocumented items; therefore, **the item name must always be written explicitly** (e.g., `FACE 0.9`) before each value.

## Structure and fields
The table has columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. It contains the following key items:

### KIND (prestressing type / side)
- **Purpose:** Selects the direction/side and the order of prestressing when multiple sides are involved.
- **Default:** `RI`
- **Possible values:**
  - `RI` = Prestressing from right
  - `LE` = Prestressing from left
  - `RILE` = Prestressing first from right, then from left
  - `LERI` = Prestressing first from left, then from right  
- **Unit:** not specified (treated as a categorical literal)

### ANWS (prestressing sequence)
- **Purpose:** Defines the sequence of actions in the prestressing process using either:
  1) A combination of literals, or  
  2) A **bit mask**.
- **Default:** `TS`, i.e. **“Stressing + Slip = TS”**
- **Mapping used by the bit mask:**
  - `1` or `T` = **Stressing**
  - `2` or `R` = **Releasing**
  - `4` or `W` = **Re-stressing**
  - `8` or `S` = **Slip**
- **Unit:** not specified (sequence encoding)
- **Example from context:** `ANWS 15` corresponds to `1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15`, i.e. all steps: stressing + releasing + re-stressing + slip.

### FAC… (force limit / stress limit factors)
This group comprises multiple factors that scale against the **reference force `ZV`** of the **SYSP** record. The table lists four factor types:

- **FAC** — *General force factor after anchor set*  
  - **Default:** `1.05`  
- **FACA** — *Maximum force factor during tensioning*  
  - **Default:** `1.18`  
- **FACE** — *Force factor at jacking anchor*  
  - **Default:** `FAC` (i.e., inherits the value of `FAC`)  
- **FACF** — *Force factor at dead anchor*  
  - **Default:** `FAC` (i.e., inherits the value of `FAC`)

Units: `—` (dimensionless scaling factors).

## Special behavior for two-sided prestressing
The provided context notes that for **two-sided prestressing**, PFAC can be repeated with a different **PFAC record** to specify a **different prestressing sequence for the second side**. In that case, both **ANWS** and the **FAC… factors** may be overridden.

## Implication for RAG storage
When indexing/extracting PFAC from text, preserve the **item-value pairing** strictly (e.g., ensure tokens like `FACE` precede numeric values). Since PFAC overwrites prior attribute records and must appear before **TEND**, it is important to treat each PFAC entry as a coherent, ordered configuration block tied to a specific `KIND` and `ANWS` combination.

The input table defines the **PDEF attribute record** parameter set, which specifies how each prestressing step is controlled on the **right and left sides**. This record is an attribute record that, per the remark in the provided context, **must be given before `TEND`** and **overwrites previously set attribute records** (`PFAC`, `PSIG`, `PAAS`, or `PDEF`). The table therefore describes the authoritative configuration for the prestressing definition that later steps (e.g., `TEND`) rely on.

### KIND (type of prestressing)
- **Item:** `KIND`
- **Meaning:** Selects the *directional order/pattern* of prestressing application.
- **Unit:** none (enumeration)
- **Default:** `RI`
- **Accepted values:**
  - `RI`: prestressing from **right**
  - `LE`: prestressing from **left**
  - `RILE`: prestressing **first from right, then from left**
  - `LERI`: prestressing **first from left, then from right**

### Step control parameters (right side)
Each parameter can represent different physical quantities depending on its numerical value. Units are shown as:
- **Unit set:** `[kN]` and `[mm]` (indicating that the underlying interpretation depends on whether the step is length-controlled or force-controlled).

Parameters on the right:
- **`STR`** – *Right stressing*
  - Default: `0`
  - Description: stress level applied during the right stressing phase.
- **`RER`** – *Right releasing*
  - Default: `0`
  - Description: right-side stress reduction or release action.
- **`RSR`** – *Right re-stressing*
  - Default: `0`
  - Description: right-side stress re-application after release.
- **`SLR`** – *Right slip*
  - Default: `0`
  - Description: slip amount associated with the right side.

### Step control parameters (left side)
Corresponding left-side parameters:
- **`STL`** – *Left stressing*
  - Default: `0`
- **`REL`** – *Left releasing*
  - Default: `0`
- **`RSL`** – *Left re-stressing*
  - Default: `0`
- **`SLL`** – *Left slip*
  - Default: `0`

### Value interpretation rule for `STR...SLL`
The context provides a key rule: the numeric values in the range
- **`< 0.0`**: interpreted as **elongations, release lengths or slip** (for that prestressing step).
- **`= 0.0`**: **deactivates** the step.
- **`(0.0, 2.0]`**: interpreted as **factors** of the reference force **`ZV`** from the `SYSP` record.
- **`> 2.0`**: interpreted as **jacking forces**.

This rule implies the table supports three operational modes per step:  
1) length-controlled behavior (negative values), 2) factor-controlled behavior (small positive values), and 3) force-controlled behavior (large positive values).

### Overall meaning
In summary, the table is a structured specification of **which prestressing operations occur** on **right and/or left** and **how each operation is quantified**, with `KIND` controlling the directional order and the parameters (`STR`, `RER`, `RSR`, `SLR`, `STL`, `REL`, `RSL`, `SLL`) controlling the actual stressing/releasing/re-stressing and slip values using the sign/range-based interpretation described above.

### Table Description: **TEND record (tendon definition and friction activation)**

This table defines the input fields for the **TEND** record, which creates a tendon associated with a duct geometry (**TGEO**) and **activates friction calculation** along that duct. It also specifies where prestressing is applied and how stations along the duct/reference axis are corrected and limited. The record assumes that **elastic shortening effects are not included** in the friction calculation.

#### Core identifiers
- **NOT**: Internal tendon ID (required).  
- **NOG**: Identifier of the duct geometry (**TGEO**) on which the tendon runs (required).  
- **NTEN**: Number of **summarized tendons** represented by this record. Default is **1**. The friction calculation is performed for a single tendon and then multiplied by **NTEN**.
- **TITL**: Human-readable tendon title (default: **LIT32** placeholder).
- **GUID**: 128-bit code in hexadecimal notation.

#### Prestressing/friction control system parameters
The friction calculation requires that related tendon/system data are already defined beforehand (notably **CS, PDAT, FRIC, PSIG, PAAS, PFAC, PDEF**).

A key conceptual parameter is **eccentricity**: if prestressing system eccentricity is not specified (**SYSP ECC = 0**), the tendon geometry coincides with the duct geometry in the corresponding segment.

#### Geometry definition and reference system selection
- **TYPE**: Selects how tendon start/end positions are interpreted:
  - **REFX** (default): positions on the **reference axis**
  - **NODE**: start/end at **beam nodes** (beams only)
  - **BEAM**: start/end at **beam elements**
  - **SPAN**: start/end span stations (TOPP span model)

The table also supports station corrections to refine the actual friction-active portion (details below).

#### Tendon location (FROM/TO) and correction offsets
- **FROM**: Start position of tendon geometry on the chosen reference (depending on **TYPE**). If not given, defaults to the duct start.
- **TO**: End position of tendon geometry. If not given, defaults to the duct end.
- **SFRO / STO**: Correction increments for **FROM** and **TO**, always expressed as increments on the **reference axis**, independent of **TYPE**.
  - The friction calculation is carried out from **(FROM + SFRO)** to **(TO + STO)**.
  - Sign matters: typically **STO is negative** when moving “back” along the positive axis direction.

Additionally, tendon length is constrained: **maximum tendon length equals duct length**; if FROM/TO lie outside the duct geometry, the tendon is shortened accordingly.

#### Effective prestressing range (EFRO/ETO)
Even though friction calculation spans **(FROM + SFRO)** to **(TO + STO)**, prestressing loads are applied only in an extended/shifted effective region:
- **EFRO / ETO**: Station increments defining the *effective prestressing* application range:
  - Prestressing loads apply from **(FROM + SFRO + EFRO)** to **(TO + STO + ETO)**.

This allows friction and load application ranges to differ.

#### Load case storage behavior
- **LC**: Load case ID for storing prestressing results.  
  - If **LC > 0**, the prestressing loads are stored and can be computed later in subsequent modules (e.g., ASE).
- **LC0** (only relevant to beams, per table text): Used for calculating **unconstrained forces** due to pure prestressing on the statically determined system. Default described as **LC** (but operational behavior is conditional, especially when **LC0 ≠ LC**).

#### Defaults and required status
The table indicates:
- **NOT** and **NOG** are required (default shown as **“!”**).
- **NTEN** defaults to **1**.
- **TYPE** defaults to **REFX**.
- **SFRO/STO/EFRO/ETO** default to **0.00**.
- **LC** defaults to **0**.
- **TITL** and **GUID** have default placeholder identifiers.

#### Summary of what the record ultimately defines
In one record, **TEND**:
1. Links a tendon to a duct geometry (**NOG/TGEO**),
2. Defines the friction-active span via **FROM/TO + SFRO/STO**,
3. Defines the prestressing load application span via **EFRO/ETO**,
4. Optionally stores results via **LC/LC0**,
5. Supports tendon summarization via **NTEN**,
6. Allows multiple reference interpretations via **TYPE** (REFX/NODE/BEAM/SPAN).

This table describes the main parameter fields for the **SLAB** record, which is used to **create a new slab tendon**. After an SLAB record is defined, the **duct geometry is established by entering support and span stations** using the related record **SLBS**. The table also notes special behavior for certain parameters depending on tendon layout type (free vs spline-generated geometry).

### Core identification and selection parameters
- **NOT** (*Number of tendon*): Identifies the tendon index. The table states that it is equivalent to “No. reference axis = No. duct geometry,” meaning **the tendon count aligns with the reference axis and duct geometry numbering**.
  - **Default shown:** `!` (unspecified/required).
- **REFS** (*Reference to the plan geometry*): Links the tendon to a plan geometry definition named **LIT4** (given as the default in the table).
  - **Default:** `LIT4`
- **NOPS** (*Number of the prestressing system*): Selects which prestressing system is used; connects tendon behavior to a predefined prestressing configuration.
  - **Default:** `!` (unspecified/required).
- **TYPG** (*Type of geometry generation*): Chooses the geometry generation method:
  - **PTFV / 1**: *Free tendon layout* (“free tendon layout (TYPG PTFV)”).
  - **PTUV / 2**: *Spline geometry generation* (analogous to PTUV/PTYV family; the table text indicates this is similar to **PTUV**).
  - **Default in table:** `PTFV`
  - **Additional context reference:** “See also: SLBS, PTUV”

### Construction stage controls
These fields define what parts of the tendon process exist at specific construction stages:
- **ICS1** (*Construction stage installation*): Default `1`.
- **ICS2** (*Construction stage grouting*): Default `1`.
- **ICS3** (*Construction stage removal*): Default `1`.
Each is a boolean-like stage activation parameter (unit shown as `–`).

### Geometry definition along the section (height offsets and lengths)
These parameters define the vertical positioning and duct path shape relative to concrete edges:
- **S0** (*Start station on the plan geometry REFS*): Starting longitudinal station.  
  - **Default:** `0.00`
- **ZSPT** (*Distance from top edge*): Height of **support points (upper layer)** measured from the **upper concrete edge**.  
  - **Default shown in table:** `0.05 m`
  - Context note: “Without a value, the middle layer is used.”
- **ZSPB** (*Distance from bottom edge*): Height of **span points (lower layer)** measured from the **lower concrete edge**.  
  - **Default:** `0.05 m`
  - Same context note about the middle layer if unset.
- **FRLT** (*Length of the straight line at supports*): Length of the straight duct section at supports in **both left and right direction**.  
  - **Default:** `0.30 m`
  - Context note: “see Figure 3.13”
- **FRLL** (*Length of the transition section*): Length over which the duct transitions **from upper to lower layer** (transition between layers).  
  - **Default:** `3.00 m`

**Important conditional note from the context:**  
“**FRLT and FRLL are only used for the free tendon layout (TYPG PTFV).**”  
So, if **TYPG is PTFV**, FRLT/FRLL drive the free layout shape; for spline-based geometry they are typically irrelevant.

### Load case and labeling
- **LC** (*Load case id; see TEND0*): Load case identifier.  
  - **Default:** `0`
- **TITL** (*Title of the tendon*): Descriptive label/name for the tendon.  
  - **Default shown:** `LIT32` (as given in the table)

Overall, this table provides the SLAB record’s parameter schema that controls **tendon indexing, linking to plan geometry, construction stage activation, vertical positioning (ZSPT/ZSPB), and free-layout duct shaping (FRLT/FRLL)**, plus metadata (LC and TITL).

The table documents the input parameters of the **SLBS** record for tendon layouts in a **SLAB** member. SLBS assigns *constraining points* (station-wise for a tendon) along the slab’s plan geometry, defining where the tendon is positioned and how its elevation/shape is controlled. A key emphasis is made for compatibility: the SLBS record may contain additional, formerly undocumented items; therefore, **the item name must always be written explicitly** (e.g., `DL <value>`), otherwise values may be misinterpreted.

### NOT (Number of tendon)
- **Meaning:** Identifies the tendon index to which the SLBS constraint data applies.  
- **Relation:** The value is tied to “no. reference axis = no. duct geometry,” meaning tendon numbering corresponds to the earlier tendon/geometry definition.
- **Unit:** none (dimensionless).
- **Default:** marked as “!” (i.e., required/not automatically set).

### BIT (bit of the constraining point)
- **Meaning:** Encodes which *type of station* a given SLBS value belongs to using a bit-coded scheme. The table lists the supported bit values:
  - `1` = **Support point**
  - `2` = **Midspan point**
  - `4` = **Start point**
  - `8` = **End point**
- **Default:** `1` (support point), but in practice the record can be extended by combining bits: e.g., a support at the end can be represented as `BIT = 1 + 8 = 9`.
- **Unit:** none (dimensionless).

### S (station on plan geometry SLAB REFS)
- **Meaning:** The longitudinal location (along the plan geometry defined by `SLAB REFS`) of the constrained point.
- **Unit:** not specified in the table excerpt (labeled “–”); it is typically a coordinate/station parameter consistent with the model’s slab reference system.
- **Default:** `S0` (start station reference).

### ZS (Position of the tendon from the edge)
- **Meaning:** Vertical positioning of the tendon relative to slab edge/top-bottom definition:
  - `ZS = 0.00` → tendon placed at the **middle layer**
  - `ZS > 0.00` → distance measured from the **top edge**
  - `ZS < 0.00` → distance measured from the **bottom edge** (negative values correspond to distance from bottom)
- **Unit:** meters `[m]`.
- **Default:** `*` (uses derived defaults if not provided).

### DZS (Inclination of the tendon in vertical direction)
- **Meaning:** Controls the vertical inclination at the constrained station, affecting how the tendon elevation transitions between points.
- **Unit:** none given for this row (listed as “–” in the excerpt; however inclination likely corresponds to a slope parameter or derived gradient).
- **Default:** `*` (default not fixed; contextual default behavior is described in the notes).

### Spline-related items: DL, DR, RV, RL
These items appear only for **spline geometry** and are referenced as “Properties of the spline geometry – see PTUV.” The table marks them with `*` and clarifies usage:
- `DL` **Straight line in negative axis direction** `[m]`
- `DR` **Straight line in positive axis direction** `[m]`
- `RV` **Vertical radius** `*` `[m]`
- `RL` **Influence length of radius** `*` `[m]`

**Important constraint:**  
The context notes additionally state that **DL, DR, RV, RH are only used with spline geometry** (SLAB `TYPG PTUV`). Therefore, these parameters should be present only when the spline geometry mode is active.

Overall, the table defines how each SLBS line specifies: **which tendon (NOT)**, **which constrained station type (BIT)**, **where along the slab (S)**, and **how the tendon is located vertically and shaped (ZS, DZS, and optionally DL/DR/RV/RL for spline)**.

The graphical representation of the prestressing is designed for a clear assignment of the tendons and not for a complete three-dimensional representation, which is reserved for the programs WinGRAF and ANIMATOR.
 For the sake of clarity, the representations are related to a horizontal projection (x-y-plane) and to a side view/elevation transverse to the reference axis (x-z-plane). Elements, ducts and tendons are ’unrolled’ along the reference axis, which is thus always a straight line – regardless of the actual curvature.
 The following input records are available for the generation of the graphical representations:
 SIZE Sheet size and scale.
 Main command for generating plan and elevation views as well as force diagrams.
 AND Linking command to combine multiple PLOTs.
 Sets colours, line widths, fill pattern and line types, or disables plot elements.
 SCHR Sets font sizes, or disabled plot elements.

The table documents configuration options related to the **SIZE** command, which controls **sheet size and scale** for generated drawings/prints. It is presented as a small specification matrix with four columns: **Item**, **Description**, **Unit**, and **Default**. The table enumerates several parameters that can be set or will be assumed by the system if not explicitly provided.

**Structure / columns**
- **Item**: short parameter identifier used in the command or UI.
- **Description**: human-readable meaning and interpretation rules.
- **Unit**: expected unit of measure where applicable.
- **Default**: what value is used when the parameter is not specified.

**Rows and meaning**
1. **TYPE**
   - **Description**: Selects the **paper size orientation/format behavior**.
     - A **positive value** means **landscape** format.
     - A **negative value** means **portrait** format.
   - **Unit**: shown as “—” (no physical unit; it is a format selector).
   - **Default**: **-URS**, indicating the default form/variant used by the system corresponds to the URS convention (consistent with the surrounding context that SIZE supports only **FORM URS**).

2. **SC**
   - **Description**: Controls the **drawing scale**.
     - **0** means **format filling** (i.e., scale chosen so content fills the available format).
     - **\*** indicates selecting the **largest possible engineering scale** automatically.
     - A numeric expression is interpreted as **1/number**, meaning scale can be specified as a rational scale denominator.
   - **Unit**: “—” (scale is represented as a special value or derived numeric meaning).
   - **Default**: **\***, i.e., choose the largest possible engineering scale by default.

3. **W**
   - **Description**: Sets the **width** of the sheet/area.
   - **Unit**: **cm**.
   - **Default**: **\***, meaning the system uses a computed/default width rather than a fixed numeric value unless overridden.

4. **H**
   - **Description**: Sets the **height** of the leaf/surface.
   - **Unit**: **cm**.
   - **Default**: **\***, meaning height is auto-determined unless explicitly set.

5. **MARG**
   - **Description**: Draws a **border** (margin/border setting).
   - **Unit**: shown as **LIT4** (a predefined border style/limit type rather than a physical unit).
   - **Default**: **\***, indicating automatic selection.

6. **FORM**
   - **Description**: Chooses the **border form** style.
   - **Unit**: **LIT4** (again, a style token/type).
   - **Default**: **\***, indicating automatic selection.

**Relevant contextual notes (from the provided text)**
- SIZE can set **sheet size and scale**; it is a basic function and was **slightly modified for the TENDON module**.
- Only **FORM URS** is supported; if TYPE/FORM is not set to **-URS/URS**, it may need to be set explicitly (or is set automatically by TENDON).
- The default behavior generally chooses the **largest possible engineering scale**, but **force diagrams** are treated specially: they are always drawn to **fill the format**.

The table therefore defines the parameter vocabulary and default/interpretation rules necessary to reproduce how the SIZE command derives paper orientation, scaling strategy (auto vs format filling vs explicit ratio), physical dimensions, and border/frame style.

The table describes the **PLOT** record parameters used to generate drawing outputs for duct geometries and tendon force/geometry representations in **plan** and **elevation** views (and optionally force diagrams). It governs *what* is drawn, *which elements* are selected, and *how* the representation is formatted with respect to axes and diagram scaling.

## Core selection control: `SHOW` / `NO`
- **`SHOW` (Selection; unit: `LIT4`, default: `TNDE`)** determines the *type of object(s) and view* to output:
  - `TNDE`: tendon in elevation view  
  - `TNDP`: tendon in plan view  
  - `GEOE`: duct in elevation view  
  - `GEOP`: duct in plan view  
  - `FACT`: force diagram
- **`NO` (ID corresponding to `SHOW`; default: `ALL`)** specifies which instance(s) are selected:
  - `ALL`: or `0` → output all ducts/tendons contained in the database (selection depends on `SHOW`)
  - `NOT`: special meaning: for `TNDE`, `TNDP` and `FACT`  
  - `NOG`: for `GEOE` and `GEOP`  
  - The context notes that **compatibility requires explicitly writing the item name before its value** (e.g., `TYPG ALL`), because the record may contain additional undocumented items.

## Representation and scaling: `FACH` and `TYPG`
- **`FACH` (Superelevation factor; default: `10`)** controls how the plot is scaled/positioned for plan/elevation views and affects force diagram depiction:
  - For the force diagram (`SHOW FACT`):
    - values **< 10.0** shift the force zero line **upwards** (“compressed representation”)
    - values **> 10.0** shift the force zero line **downwards** (“stretched representation”)
- **`TYPG` (Type of representation; default: `ALL`)** selects what geometry components are drawn:
  - `DUCT`: duct only  
  - `TEND`: tendon only  
  - `DUTE`: duct and tendon together  
  - `ALL`: draws *duct plus reference and gravity axis*

## Drawing limits: `FROM` / `TO`
- **`FROM` (Station start; default: `*`)** defines the starting station for the plan/elevation output.
- **`TO` (Station end; default: `*`)** defines the end station.
- The context states that for plan/elevation views, by default the limits are taken from the underlying **duct and tendon curve extents**; `FROM/TO` override this.

## Tendon overview: `PCS`
- **`PCS` (Tendon overview; default: `0`)** controls whether additional tendon definition domains are shown:
  - `0`: don’t show
  - `≠ 0`: show tendon overview
- Applies particularly to **plan/elevation views**: when enabled, the tendon definition domains are drawn.

## How the record behaves (context summary)
- Plan and elevation views reference the **reference axis**, drawn as a straight line; ducts/tendons are “unrolled” along this axis for plotting.
- Compared modes: with `GEOP/ GEOE` the entire duct and its tendons are drawn, whereas with `TNDP/ TNDE` only the **duct section where the tendon is defined** is drawn.
- The record supports selecting either a specific duct geometry ID or tendon ID; alternately `0`/`ALL` can output all relevant items.

Overall, this table defines the parameters needed to precisely control selection (`SHOW` + `NO`), output scaling (`FACH`), content composition (`TYPG`), range (`FROM/TO`), and optional tendon domain visualization (`PCS`) for generated duct/tendon plots.

Each row maps a specific **semantic element** that may appear in the graphical output to its **default configuration value**. The table has five columns:

- **Item**: Identifier for the element to be configured, ranging from **F1** to **F14**.
- **Description**: Human-readable meaning of what the element represents in the diagram/output.
- **Unit**: Measurement unit column; for all listed items it is shown as **“—”**, indicating that these settings are not physical quantities requiring units (they are likely style/visibility selectors, series selectors, or integer-coded plot parameters).
- **Default**: The default numeric code used if no explicit value is provided.
- (Implicitly) **Description corresponds directly to the Item**, so downstream consumers can interpret numeric codes semantically.
